meta.what: Amounts of Russian assets frozen, per holding country: Bank of Russia reserves immobilised (cbr_eur) and private assets of sanctioned persons and entities frozen (private_eur); EU and G7/REPO totals; windfall, ERA and reparations-loan facts. For explainer pages and search; not wired into the pipeline.
meta.units: EUR bn. v = the figure shown (latest official where one exists, converted at about the rate of its date; native gives the original), lo/hi = range across sources, date = date of v, src = source ids (first = v's source; resolved in 'sources'), official = whether v comes from a government, EU institution, central bank or the holder itself. v null = no public figure; est = an outside estimate, to be shown only as one.
meta.rule: Stocks only. The site's 'Russian money frozen' line counts the return Russia lost on these stocks (frozen_assets.json, private_frozen_r39.json); never the stock itself.
meta.reuse: Amounts from rounds 7 and 39 are reused and updated: UK central-bank estimate (now ~GBP 8bn press figure, was a guess of 10), Switzerland (June 2026), Euroclear (June 2026), Luxembourg (official 'below EUR 10,000'), France (LCP 2026), Latvia, Sweden, Finland, Estonia, Lithuania, Poland, Czechia added.

BEL.name: Belgium (Euroclear Bank, Brussels)

cbr_eur.basis: Commission figure used for the reparations-loan and Art. 122 texts: about EUR 185bn of the EUR 210bn of Bank of Russia assets in the EU sit at Euroclear. Euroclear's CEO gave 180 of 193 (Oct 2025); EPRS/PISM 180. The value at the freeze (Feb 2022) is not published.

company_figure.what: Euroclear Bank's balance sheet: sanctioned Russian assets (cash, Bank of Russia plus private), EUR bn
company_figure.note: This is the sanctioned cash on Euroclear's balance sheet, rising as frozen bonds mature into cash. It is the figure behind headlines like 'Euroclear passes EUR 200bn'. It includes private sanctioned cash (about EUR 13bn) and is not the same as the Bank of Russia's position.

private_eur.basis: Belgian Treasury (via OCCRP, Feb 2025): EUR 65bn of frozen assets beside EUR 193bn of blocked Bank of Russia transactions; of the 65, about EUR 10bn belongs to sanctioned Russian banks and EUR 55bn are securities that passed through the sanctioned depository NSD (mostly owned by unsanctioned Russian investors). Belgium reported EUR 3.5bn of sanctioned persons' assets to the Commission (Dec 2022), the most of any member then.

nsd_blocked_securities.note: Russian investors' securities blocked at Euroclear because the NSD is sanctioned. Not sanctioned persons' assets in the usual sense; shown separately.

BEL.notes: Belgium hosts most of the world's immobilised Russian reserves because Euroclear is the main international depository for the bonds central banks hold. The freeze is an EU decision; Euroclear only holds the assets. Euroclear's cash in Canadian dollars, sterling and Australian dollars (about 8%, 17% and 2%) sits with banks abroad but is Euroclear's, i.e. Belgium's, not Canada's, the UK's or Australia's.

FRA.name: France

cbr_eur.basis: The only official figure: finance minister Le Maire, EUR 22.8bn of Bank of Russia assets immobilised (March 2022). The government has declined to update it (Euronews, Nov 2025). Later estimates: 19 (EPRS/PISM 2025; LCP, May 2026), about 18 (press). Held by commercial banks.

private_eur.basis: LCP (May 2026): 'nearly EUR 1bn' of oligarchs' assets frozen in France (no official source named). Commission list, Dec 2022: EUR 1.3bn (mostly property); the Treasury's 2022 total of 23.7 less the 22.8 central-bank figure gives 0.9. No recent Treasury figure found.

FRA.notes: France is the second holder of Bank of Russia assets in the EU, in commercial banks it has not named.

GBR.name: United Kingdom

cbr_eur.basis: No official figure: the government declines to give one. The Times (5 Dec 2025) and the FT (11 Dec 2025) report about GBP 8bn of Russian sovereign assets in UK banks (about EUR 9bn). EPRS/PISM's EUR 26.6bn probably counts Euroclear's sterling cash, which is Belgium's.

private_eur.basis: OFSI Annual Review 2024-25: GBP 28.7bn reported frozen under the Russia regime by May 2025 (GBP 22.5bn in the 2024 frozen-asset review; 'over GBP 25bn', HM Treasury, March 2025). Values as reported at designation; excludes sovereign assets (Euronews).

GBR.notes: OFSI's figure is the largest national private figure published anywhere. No 2025-26 review was found by 27 Oct 2026.

CHE.name: Switzerland

CHE.notes: The only country that publishes both figures regularly, and keeps them apart.

private_eur.basis: No US figure published. REPO's 'more than USD 58bn' (March 2023) covers all members together.

JPN.name: Japan

no_public_figure.what: Countries with Russia sanctions in force for which no public amount was found (central bank or private)
no_public_figure.note: Absence of a figure is not evidence of zero. Singapore and South Korea banned transactions with the Bank of Russia in March 2022 but published no amount. Liechtenstein, Iceland and Norway apply EU-type sanctions; no amounts found in this round.

eu_cbr.basis: Commission: about EUR 210bn of Bank of Russia assets immobilised in the EU, of which about 185 at Euroclear and about 25 in commercial banks (France, Germany, Sweden, Cyprus, Belgium). The basis of the reparations-loan proposal (3 Dec 2025) and of Regulation 2025/2600.

eu_private.basis: Commission: 'more than EUR 28 billion of private assets in the EU frozen' (sanctioned persons and entities); 18.9 at 16 Dec 2022, 24.1 by mid-2023. Does not include the EUR 55bn of NSD-blocked securities at Euroclear.

repo_cbr.basis: REPO task force: about USD 280bn of Russian sovereign assets immobilised in REPO jurisdictions (EU, G7, Australia), the majority in the EU; the latest official all-country total. Experts and the Bank of Russia say USD 300-330bn.

repo_private.basis: REPO: more than USD 58bn of sanctioned Russians' assets blocked or frozen by all members. No later REPO total.

countries_with_figure_cbr.note: Sum of the per-country values above (estimates used for Germany, the UK and Japan; Canada and Australia zero, see their notes). Mixed dates. EU about 208 against the Commission's 210; with the UK (~9), Switzerland, US and Japan (~28) about EUR 255bn, consistent with REPO's USD 280bn (EUR 260bn at the 2023 rate).

countries_with_figure_private.note: Sum of the national private figures above (Belgium's sanctioned banks, not the NSD securities). Mixed dates (2022-2026). The EU sum (about 30) is close to the Commission's 'more than 28bn', but by luck: Belgium's 10 is the Treasury's sanctioned-banks figure (the Commission's list had 3.5), while many members' figures are old (2022-23) or missing.

windfall.what: EU windfall contribution: net profits Euroclear (and other CSDs) earn on the Bank of Russia's immobilised cash, paid to the EU. The assets themselves are not touched.
windfall.conflicts: Tranche sizes differ slightly between Euroclear (1.55, about 2.1, 1.6) and Commission or press rounding (1.5, 1.5-1.6). Euroclear's 'about EUR 6.6bn to date' (17 Jul 2026) plus the 1.4bn of 3 Aug 2026 gives the Commission's 'about EUR 8bn'.
windfall.belgium: Belgium also taxes Euroclear's Russia-related profit (corporate tax about EUR 1.7bn for 2024) and has pledged that money to Ukraine.

era_loans.what: G7 Extraordinary Revenue Acceleration loans: about USD 50bn (EUR 45bn) lent to Ukraine in 2024-2025, repaid from the windfall revenues of the immobilised assets, not from the assets.
era_loans.status: The EU paid its first EUR 3bn on 10 Jan 2025 and its share was to be paid by end-2025; the UK paid its last tranche in April 2025. Reports in 2026 said parts of the US and Japanese shares were still being paid out. Not checked in full this round.

reparations_loan.status_2026_10: Not adopted. Proposed by the Commission (idea Sep 2025, EUR 140bn; legal proposal 3 Dec 2025 with up to EUR 210bn of immobilised assets). Set aside on 19 Dec 2025 in favour of the EUR 90bn Ukraine Support Loan from EU borrowing; leaders asked for work on it to continue. Revived by several members for 2027 in Aug-Oct 2026; no decision at the 15-16 Oct 2026 summit.
reparations_loan.mechanism: The EU would borrow the cash balances that Euroclear and other institutions hold for the Bank of Russia (Euroclear would get an interest-free EU debt claim instead), and lend that money to Ukraine. Ukraine would repay only if Russia pays reparations; the Bank of Russia's claim on Euroclear would stay, and Member States would guarantee the EU against it being enforced. Not a confiscation.
reparations_loan.belgium_role: Euroclear holds about EUR 185bn of the EUR 210bn in the EU, so Belgium carries most of the legal and retaliation risk (Russian court claims against Euroclear; the 2015 Belgium-Russia investment treaty). Belgium's PM De Wever demanded shared liability, guarantees and the participation of the other holders (France's banks, Japan, the UK); he also called confiscation unacceptable. Italy, Malta and Bulgaria, and less openly France, backed Belgium's caution.
reparations_loan.what_was_agreed_instead: Ukraine Support Loan, EUR 90bn for 2026-27 (indicatively 30 budget support, 60 defence), EU borrowing guaranteed by budget headroom, 24 members (without CZ, HU, SK). Repaid by Ukraine only out of reparations; the EU 'reserves its right' to use the immobilised assets to repay it.

timeline.fact: The EU, US, UK, Canada, Japan and Switzerland bar transactions with the Bank of Russia; its reserves in their jurisdictions are immobilised (EU: Council Regulation 2022/334 amending 833/2014).
REPO task force: more than USD 58bn of sanctioned Russians' private assets blocked or frozen.
REPO task force maps about USD 280bn of immobilised Russian sovereign assets, mostly in the EU.
EU windfall contribution: CSDs holding over EUR 1m of Bank of Russia assets pay most of their net profit on that cash to the EU (Regulation 2024/1469). The principal is untouched.

G7 Apulia summit: about USD 50bn of 'Extraordinary Revenue Acceleration' (ERA) loans to Ukraine, to be serviced from the windfall revenues; the assets stay immobilised until Russia pays for the damage.
First windfall payment from Euroclear, about EUR 1.55bn (Commission: EUR 1.5bn); 90% via the European Peace Facility, 10% via the Ukraine Facility (also for the second tranche).

EU ERA share set up: Ukraine Loan Cooperation Mechanism and up to EUR 18.1bn macro-financial assistance (Regulation 2024/2773). Other lenders: US USD 20bn, UK GBP 2.26bn, Canada CAD 5bn, Japan JPY 471.9bn.
Commission pays the first EUR 3bn of the EU's ERA share.
Windfall payments: about EUR 2.1bn (spring) and 1.6bn (summer); from the third tranche 95% goes to the Ukraine Loan Cooperation Mechanism (repaying the ERA loans) and 5% to the EPF.
Commission floats a EUR 140bn 'reparations loan' from the cash balances at Euroclear (about EUR 45bn of the 185 already backing ERA).
European Council does not agree; Belgium asks for shared liability and guarantees; Commission asked for options.

Commission tables legal proposals: a reparations loan using up to EUR 210bn of immobilised assets, or EU borrowing, to cover two-thirds of Ukraine's EUR 135bn needs for 2026-27 (EUR 90bn); plus an Art. 122 regulation to block transfers back to Russia.
Council Regulation (EU) 2025/2600 (Art. 122 TFEU, qualified majority): immobilised Bank of Russia assets may not be transferred back to Russia; no six-monthly unanimous renewal any more.

European Council: EUR 90bn loan for 2026-27 from EU borrowing backed by budget headroom, not from the assets. Ukraine repays only once it receives reparations; the assets stay immobilised and the Union 'reserves its right' to use them to repay the loan; work on the Reparations Loan to continue. Czechia, Hungary and Slovakia stay out (enhanced cooperation).
Council position on the EUR 90bn Ukraine Support Loan (Regulation (EU) 2026/467).
The Bank of Russia challenges Regulation 2025/2600 before the EU General Court.
Council adopts the last act for the EUR 90bn loan after Hungary lifts its veto (tied to the Druzhba restart).
Moscow court rules for the Bank of Russia against Euroclear; appeal rejected 16 Jul 2026. Euroclear does not recognise the jurisdiction; such rulings are not recognised under EU law.
First Ukraine Support Loan payment, EUR 3.2bn (and EUR 3.9bn for drones on 30 June). EUR 19.8bn disbursed by late October 2026 (Commission page).
Euroclear: EUR 202bn of its EUR 241bn balance sheet relates to sanctioned Russian assets; H1 interest EUR 2.3bn; about EUR 6.6bn paid as windfall so far.

Fifth windfall payment, EUR 1.4bn; about EUR 8bn in all since 2024. The Commission counts EUR 3.8bn of EU support to Ukraine 'from the proceeds of Russian immobilised assets' (the EPF and Ukraine Facility parts; the ULCM part repays ERA).

Sweden, the Netherlands, Poland and Spain push to revive the reparations loan for 2027; the ECB warns about confidence in the euro. European Council 15-16 Oct 2026: no decision, will 'revert to the issue in a timely manner'.

phrasing.rule: The site counts the yearly return Russia lost on these assets (Russian money frozen line), never the frozen stock. Amounts on pages are context: 'frozen' or 'immobilised', not 'lost', 'taken' or 'seized'.
do: Belgium: 'About EUR 185bn of the Russian central bank's reserves are immobilised at Euroclear in Brussels (European Commission, December 2025). Euroclear reports EUR 202bn of sanctioned Russian assets on its balance sheet (30 June 2026), most of it the central bank's cash.'
EU: 'About EUR 210bn of Bank of Russia assets are immobilised in the EU, and more than EUR 28bn of sanctioned Russians' private assets are frozen (European Commission).'
Countries without a figure: 'Japan has not published how much it holds; estimates are EUR 20-40bn.' / 'No official figure has been published.'
Ownership: 'The assets still belong to Russia's central bank; only the income is used (windfall contribution, ERA loans).'
The reparations loan: 'proposed, not adopted'; the EUR 90bn loan 'from EU borrowing, to be repaid by Ukraine only if Russia pays reparations'.
dont: Do not add the EPRS figures for Canada (15.1) and the UK (26.6) to Belgium's: they include Euroclear's cash in those currencies.
Do not add Euroclear's EUR 202bn and the Commission's EUR 185bn: they overlap.
Do not mix the private EUR 28bn (sanctioned persons) with the EUR 55bn of NSD-blocked securities at Euroclear.
Do not present the EUR 90bn Ukraine Support Loan as funded by Russian assets, or the windfall payments as the assets themselves.
Do not show the frozen stock as Russia's loss, cost or the country's gain.
